Tuesday, 9 pm
Gopika: how was the review
Sangeeta: he called me "the backbone of the team" 🙂
Sangeeta: then handed me the Kolkata vendor audit. on top of the two I already have
Gopika: that's the third extra thing this month no?
Sangeeta: yes. he said people who really care don't count hours
Sangeeta: I felt proud for a second and then I felt weird
Gopika: weird how
Sangeeta: like the praise is the salary 😅
Gopika: what does your offer letter say about scope
Sangeeta: checking
Sangeeta: the audit isn't in it
Sangeeta: I'll email him tonight. happy to take it if we agree what comes off my plate and by when
Gopika: good. keep it in writing

qa.q: What extra task did the manager hand Sangeeta after the review?
Why did Sangeeta feel weird after feeling proud?
qa.a: Sangeeta began to suspect the praise was standing in for pay, since the manager linked caring about the team to not counting hours.

qa.q: What does Sangeeta plan to send the manager, and why is it useful?
qa.a: An email offering to take the audit if they agree what comes off the plate and by when, which sets the scope in writing.

qa.q: How might the manager see his own request?
qa.a: He may think he is offering trust and recognition, even though the effect is that Sangeeta carries unpaid hours.

grounding: A manager pairs praise with extra work and hints that loyalty means unpaid hours; the worker feels flattered and trapped, then sets limits in writing.

passage:
"Mohit, you're my star," Ayesha said on Friday at seven, dropping a new file on his desk at the Nariman Point office. "Only you can handle this client. I know you won't let me down."

He felt the warm glow. Then the weight. It was his fourth weekend in a row. His contract said forty-five hours a week; last week he'd done sixty-two. Ayesha never mentioned overtime pay, only loyalty. "People who go the extra mile get noticed," she liked to say.

On the train home Mohit counted: three promotions in the team this year, none for the "stars" who worked weekends.

On Monday he wrote an email, calm and short. "Thank you for trusting me with the Mehra account. To do it well, I'd like to agree the scope. I can deliver the report by Thursday within normal hours. Weekend work would need to be agreed separately."

His stomach was in knots when he pressed send. Ayesha replied an hour later: "Noted. Thursday is fine."

qa.q: How many hours did Mohit work last week?
How did Mohit feel when Ayesha called him her star?
qa.a: Mohit felt flattered and warm at first, and then weighed down and trapped by the extra work.

qa.q: How did Mohit set a limit wisely?
qa.a: He noticed praise was being used instead of pay, then thanked Ayesha, clarified the scope in writing and said weekend work needed separate agreement.

qa.q: How does Ayesha seem to see Mohit's extra hours?
qa.a: Ayesha seems to treat his extra hours as proof of loyalty rather than work that should be paid or limited.

grounding: The passage shows a young man whose manager uses praise and talk of loyalty to pile on unpaid hours, who feels flattered and trapped, sets limits and clarifies scope in writing.

passage:
"Sarita, you're the only one I can count on," Darshan said, leaning on her cubicle. "The Diwali catalogue. Can you take the photo edits too?"

"The photo edits? That's Kiran's work."

"Kiran's not like you. You're family here." He smiled. "Family doesn't count hours."

Sarita felt the glow and the trap at the same time. "Darshan, I'm already doing the copy and the layout. That's twelve-hour days."

"It's just for this month."

"You said that in August."

He laughed. "Loyal people get rewarded in the end."

"When? And how?" She kept her voice light. "I'd like to know what the reward is. In writing, if it's real."

He blinked. "You're being very formal."

"I'm being clear. I'll finish the copy and layout by Friday. The photo edits need to go back to Kiran, or we move the deadline."

A long pause. "Fine. Kiran does the photos."

Sarita typed a one-line email confirming it, and sent it before he reached his desk.

qa.q: Whose work were the photo edits normally?
qa.a: The photo edits were Kiran's work.

qa.q: How did Sarita feel when Darshan called her family?
qa.a: Sarita felt flattered and trapped at the same time, the glow and the pressure mixed.

qa.q: How did Sarita respond to praise used as pay?
qa.a: She asked what the reward actually was and asked for it in writing, set a clear limit on her tasks, and confirmed the agreement by email.

qa.q: How did Darshan react when Sarita set her limit?
qa.a: Darshan seemed surprised and a little put out, calling her formal, before agreeing to give the photos back to Kiran.

grounding: A dialogue shows a young woman whose manager uses praise and "family" talk to pile on unpaid work, who notices it, sets limits and clarifies scope in writing.
